title: HIW Partial Tuition Fee Waiver for non-EEA citizens
program_type: Tuition-fee remission scholarship: a university faculty/faculty-institute partial tuition fee waiver, awarded first-come first-served to the first eligible applicants after admission
funding_type: Tuition fee remission only (partial waiver of the increased non-EEA tuition fee)
administering_authority: KU Leuven Institute of Philosophy (Hoger Instituut voor Wijsbegeerte, HIW), KU Leuven
implementing_agency: Education and Students Office of the KU Leuven Institute of Philosophy
programme_action: KU Leuven partial tuition fee waiver for non-EEA citizens - Institute of Philosophy procedure (nationality-restricted, DAC least developed / other low income countries)
description: The HIW Partial Tuition Fee Waiver for non-EEA citizens is administered by the KU Leuven Institute of Philosophy and listed in the KU Leuven scholarship catalogue. It is a partial tuition fee waiver for students admitted to the Bachelor of Philosophy, Master of Philosophy or Research Master of Philosophy at KU Leuven whose nationality appears on the Institute's eligible-nationality list, which is derived from the OECD DAC list of ODA recipients (least developed countries and other low income countries). Recipients pay a reduced tuition fee instead of the increased fee normally charged to non-EEA students; in academic year 2026-2027 this reduced fee was EUR 3,252.72 for a full-time programme of 60 ECTS, against EUR 9,493.90 for non-EEA students. Only three waivers are offered per academic year and they are granted to the first three eligible applicants who submit a complete request by email after receiving their admission letter.

award_types: Partial tuition fee waiver (reduced tuition fee)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: A single award type: a partial waiver of the increased tuition fee charged to non-EEA students. Recipients of the 2026-2027 cycle paid EUR 3,252.72 for a full-time 60-ECTS programme instead of the EUR 9,493.90 non-EEA rate. The Institute of Philosophy runs a separate Study Support Allowance (full tuition fee reimbursement plus a EUR 1,500 lump sum) and a Refugee Scholarship, but these are different awards and are not part of this scheme.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Applicants with a nationality of a DAC 'least developed country' or 'other low income country' receive the waiver for the entire length of the programme, including the first year. The Institute of Philosophy tuition fees page states that award holders keep the waiver for the entire duration of their studies at the Institute and that the tuition fee is reduced to the EEA rate applicable in the year of registration, adjusted if the EEA rate changes. The scholarship catalogue page states a base duration of one academic year, so the renewal rule should be confirmed with the Education and Students Office for individual cases.
programme_structure.intake: One main intake per academic year, starting in September. KU Leuven states that a second-semester (February) intake is not possible for the Institute of Philosophy programmes. Applicants must first gain admission through the KU Leuven application tool; the waiver request itself is submitted by email only after the admission letter has been issued.

status_note: The 2026-2027 application window closed on 20 September 2026 at 01:00 (GMT+1), so that cycle is closed. The 2027-2028 window opened on 1 October 2026 at 01:00 (GMT+1) and closes on 20 September 2027 at 01:00 (GMT+1), so the award is currently open for the next entry. Because the waiver can only be requested after an admission letter is issued, an applicant must also fit the relevant programme's admission window; the non-EEA admission deadline for the Institute of Philosophy programmes was 1 March in the 2026-2027 cycle, and the 2027-2028 admission windows had not been published for all programmes at the time of verification.
verification_notes: All figures in this record were transcribed from official KU Leuven pages read on 2026-10-03: the 2027-2028 and 2026-2027 versions of the HIW Partial Tuition Fee Waiver page in the KU Leuven scholarship catalogue, the Institute of Philosophy tuition fees page, the Bachelor of Philosophy admission-requirements page in the KU Leuven programme guide, and the KU Leuven tuition fee regulations 2026-2027. Twelve official-source fetches were completed. Unresolved items are recorded in verification.programme_check_required and verification.unverified_or_removed_claims: the 2027-2028 reduced fee amount is published only as 'to be communicated'; two official pages state the waiver duration differently (one academic year on the catalogue page versus the entire duration of studies on the Institute page); English test minima are published at programme level rather than on the award page; and Ghent University publishes no bachelor's-level international scholarship, with its reduced-tuition-fee route closed to newly arriving non-EEA students by the Flemish nationality conditions.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: 1 October (year before entry) to 20 September (year of entry), closing at 01:00 (GMT+1)
application_deadline.application_period: 2027-2028 cycle: opens 1 October 2026 at 01:00 (GMT+1); closes 20 September 2027 at 01:00 (GMT+1). The preceding 2026-2027 cycle ran 1 October 2025 to 20 September 2026 at 01:00 (GMT+1) and is closed.
application_deadline.official_rule: The KU Leuven scholarship catalogue publishes an exact calendar deadline of 20 September 2027 at 01:00 (GMT+1) for the 2027-2028 academic year (the 2026-2027 page published 20 September 2026 at 01:00 (GMT+1)). No additional separate deadline applies to the waiver request itself, but the applicant must already hold a KU Leuven admission offer when submitting the request, so the programme admission deadline is the binding date in practice.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Deadlines are published per academic year on cycle-specific pages, so the exact date must be re-read on the next cycle page before relying on it. Because only three waivers exist and they go to the first three complete eligible requests, submitting on the deadline date is not sufficient - late-comers in the same year receive nothing.

programme_duration.official_range: Bachelor of Philosophy (Leuven): 180 ECTS, full-time, three academic years. The Institute of Philosophy also lists abridged Bachelor of Philosophy programmes of 63 and 102 ECTS.
programme_duration.renewal_note: The waiver, not the degree, is what renews. Students with an eligible DAC nationality receive the partial fee waiver for the entire length of the programme, including the first year, and the reduced fee tracks the EEA rate applicable in the year of registration. The scholarship catalogue page states a base duration of one academic year; the Institute of Philosophy tuition fees page states the waiver is held for the entire duration of studies at the Institute.

funding.scholarship_type: Partial tuition fee waiver (tuition fee remission)
funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly allowance or stipend is published for this award. It is a tuition fee reduction only.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel support is published in the official source for this waiver.
funding.fully_funded_note: Not fully funded. The waiver only reduces tuition fees. Recipients of the 2026-2027 cycle still paid EUR 3,252.72 for a 60-ECTS full-time programme, which is higher than the EEA rate of EUR 1,181.40, and no living costs, travel, insurance, installation or accommodation support is provided by this award.

tuition.conditions: Partial tuition fee waiver. In academic year 2026-2027 recipients paid a reduced tuition fee of EUR 3,252.72 for a full-time programme of 60 ECTS, against EUR 9,493.90 charged to non-EEA students and EUR 1,181.40 charged to EEA students (KU Leuven Institute of Philosophy tuition fees page, 2026-2027). The waiver therefore removes part, but not all, of the increased non-EEA fee: the reduction is EUR 6,241.18 per year on the 2026-2027 60-ECTS rate (derived by subtracting the two published fees; this difference is not published by KU Leuven as an award value). The 2027-2028 amount is published only as 'to be communicated'.

travel_allowance.note: Not published in official source for this waiver

installation_allowance.note: Not published in official source for this waiver

visa_support.note: Not published in official source for this waiver

insurance.note: Not published as part of this award. Separately, the KU Leuven tuition fee regulations 2026-2027 state that the tuition fee includes affiliation with the collective accident insurance and the civil liability insurance for study-related activities, and that affiliation with the 'private life civil liability' insurance is an additional obligation for students with a non-EEA nationality temporarily residing in Belgium.

accommodation_support.note: Not published in official source for this waiver

bond.note: No bond, service obligation or return-to-home-country condition is published in the official source for this waiver.

total_estimated_value.note: The official source does not publish a total award value, and the waiver is a per-academic-year conditional tuition fee reduction rather than a lump-sum grant, so a total value is not computed here.

coverage: Partial tuition fee remission for a full-time programme of 60 ECTS: EUR 3,252.72 payable instead of the EUR 9,493.90 non-EEA tuition fee in academic year 2026-2027 (a derived reduction of EUR 6,241.18 for that year)
The waiver is retained for the entire length of the programme, including the first year, for students whose nationality is classified as a DAC least developed country or other low income country
No living allowance, travel, insurance, installation or accommodation support
coverage_limitations: Tuition fees only: the award does not cover living costs, travel, insurance, installation or accommodation.
Partial, not full, remission: the 2026-2027 recipient fee of EUR 3,252.72 is higher than the EEA rate of EUR 1,181.40, so recipients still pay more than EEA students.
Only three waivers per academic year, awarded first-come first-served to the first three complete eligible requests; eligibility does not guarantee an award.

Nationality-locked to DAC least developed countries and other low income countries. Students from lower-middle-income countries and territories are explicitly not eligible, so the large majority of non-EEA nationalities do not qualify.
The waiver can only be requested after a KU Leuven admission letter has been issued; it cannot be applied for in advance of admission.
The exact fee reduction for academic year 2027-2028 is not published and is stated only as 'to be communicated'; the 2026-2027 figures are the last published rates.

The scholarship catalogue page states a duration of one academic year while the Institute of Philosophy tuition fees page states the waiver runs for the entire duration of studies; the two official pages are not identical and the per-case renewal rule should be confirmed.
Fee amounts are subject to annual indexation and may differ from the published 2026-2027 figures in later years.
eligible_applicants: Non-EEA nationals holding a nationality on the Institute of Philosophy eligible-nationality list (DAC least developed countries and other low income countries)
Applicants admitted to the Bachelor of Philosophy (Leuven), the Master of Philosophy (Leuven) or the Research Master of Philosophy (Leuven) at KU Leuven
Students resuming studies after an interruption, if they continue to meet the eligibility criteria (they must notify the Institute of Philosophy of their return and eligibility by email)
EEA nationals are explicitly not eligible for this waiver
final_year_condition: This award funds a bachelor's degree, so the qualifying prior qualification is secondary education rather than a completed bachelor's degree: the Institute of Philosophy considers applications from all students holding a high school diploma that gives access to university-level education in their home country. The official award page does not explicitly address applicants still in their final year of secondary school, and because the waiver request can only be submitted after an admission letter has been issued, an applicant must hold at least a conditional admission before requesting the waiver. Applicants in their final secondary-school year should confirm with the Education and Students Office whether a conditional admission offer can be used to request the waiver.
equivalent_degree_note: Yes. The Institute of Philosophy considers applications from all students holding a high school diploma that gives access to university-level education in their home country, and students may be admitted by the Board of Admissions on the basis of the complete application file. Within Flanders, general bachelor admission requirements also accept a Flemish short-course higher education degree, a Flemish higher education for social advancement degree (excluding the certificate of pedagogic aptitude), a Flemish HBO degree or certificate, or a Flemish bachelor's or master's degree.

age_limit.official_source: No age limit is published for the HIW Partial Tuition Fee Waiver or for the Bachelor of Philosophy admission requirements.

nationality_quota: Three waivers per academic year, allocated first-come first-served among eligible non-EEA students from DAC least developed or other low income countries. No country-by-country sub-quota is published.

eligibility.citizenship: Non-EEA nationality required. The applicant's nationality must be on the Institute of Philosophy list: Africa (Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Niger, Rwanda, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia); Asia (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, North Korea, Nepal, Syria, Timor-Leste, Yemen); Central America (Haiti); Oceania (Kiribati, Solomon Islands, Tuvalu). EEA students are not eligible.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No Belgian residence requirement. The list is based on nationality and is derived from the OECD DAC list of ODA recipients (least developed countries and other low income countries); students from lower-middle-income countries and territories are not eligible.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: A high school diploma that gives access to university-level education in the applicant's home country. Admission is decided by the Board of Admissions on the complete application file, including the Institute of Philosophy academic reading and writing assignment, and is based on the candidate's academic potential.
eligibility.academic_requirements: The applicant must meet the admission requirements set for the eligible programme. Students must have been admitted to the Bachelor, Master or Research Master of Philosophy (full or abridged) and must hold an official KU Leuven admission letter before applying for the waiver.
eligibility.language_requirement: English proficiency is required. Accepted proofs: TOEFL (internet-based or paper delivered) minimum 90 overall with no subscore below 18 (or the new TOEFL scale as of 21/01/2026: Reading 4, Listening 4, Speaking 3.5, Writing 4); Academic IELTS minimum 6.5 with no subscore below 5.5; ESOL Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) 176 with no subscore below 162, or C2 Proficiency. Taking a test is recommended but not required. Exemption is granted only for degrees obtained in Australia, English-speaking Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom or the USA, provided the entire study was completed in English; online degrees do not qualify.
eligibility.financial_need: The Institute states that it awards partial tuition fee waivers to students from non-EEA countries in need of financial support. The operative eligibility test, however, is nationality on the DAC list: no income test, means test or financial documentation is published for this waiver.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: The applicant must already be admitted to an eligible programme at the time the waiver request is submitted. Students resuming studies after an interruption remain eligible if they meet the criteria.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Restricted to programmes of the Institute of Philosophy: Bachelor of Philosophy, Master of Philosophy and Research Master of Philosophy.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No minimum percentage, GPA or grade threshold is published for the waiver or for admission to the Bachelor of Philosophy. Admission is assessed on the complete application file.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Philosophy requires a high school diploma giving access to university-level education in the home country plus submission of an application file to the Institute of Philosophy consisting of a CV, a motivation letter and the Institute of Philosophy academic reading and writing assignment. Students who obtained their prior degree at an institution of the Flemish Community apply under the general Flemish bachelor admission requirements.
selection_factors_may_include: Academic potential as demonstrated by the complete application file
The Institute of Philosophy academic reading and writing assignment
Timeliness of the waiver request (first three complete eligible requests are awarded)
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: The waiver itself has no competitive academic selection: the first three eligible applicants who submit a complete request are awarded it. Academic assessment applies only to programme admission, and the selection criteria of the waiver are stated to be the same as those of the corresponding programme.

english_requirement.moi_rule: An exemption from the English proficiency test is granted only to applicants holding a degree obtained in Australia, English-speaking Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom or the USA, provided they can prove the entire study was completed in English. Degrees obtained in an online format cannot serve as a basis for an exemption. KU Leuven states that taking an English proficiency test is recommended but not required, while English proficiency itself is required.
english_requirement.test_score_note: Scores are published on the Bachelor of Philosophy admission-requirements page (programme level), not on the award page itself. Published minima: TOEFL internet-based or paper-delivered 90 overall with no subscore below 18, or the new TOEFL score scale as of 21/01/2026 (Reading 4, Listening 4, Speaking 3.5, Writing 4); Academic IELTS 6.5 with no subscore below 5.5; ESOL Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) 176 with no subscore below 162, or C2 Proficiency. No PTE or Duolingo minimum is published. No test-validity period in months is published.

language_of_instruction.bilingual_programmes: The Bachelor of Philosophy is taught in English at the Institute of Philosophy and the same programme is also available in Dutch. The Institute recommends the Dutch-language bachelor programme for applicants whose mother tongue is Dutch.
language_of_instruction.language_note: The eligible programme covered by this record, the Bachelor of Philosophy (Leuven), is an English-taught 180-ECTS programme, so English proficiency is required.

application_method.application_route: Two-stage: first apply for admission to the Bachelor of Philosophy, Master of Philosophy or Research Master of Philosophy through the KU Leuven application tool (non-EEA admission deadline 1 March in the 2026-2027 cycle); then, after receiving the admission letter, email the Institute of Philosophy Education and Students Office with the admission offer (PDF) attached, stating full name, student number, nationality and programme of admission.
application_steps: Apply for admission to an eligible programme through the KU Leuven application tool, using the standard application form and the requested core documents plus the Institute of Philosophy academic reading and writing assignment, CV and motivation letter.
Receive the formal KU Leuven admission letter (Letter of Admission).

After admission, email the Institute of Philosophy Education and Students Office with the admission offer attached as a PDF, stating full name, student number, nationality and the programme of admission.
The Education and Students Office checks nationality against the eligible list and completeness of the request.
One of the three waivers is awarded to one of the first three eligible applicants submitting a complete request.
The reduced tuition fee is applied to the student's invoice at registration.
application_method.application_fee: Not published for this waiver. KU Leuven charges a processing fee for admission applications (recognised refugees in Belgium are among the exempt categories); the official figures must be checked on the current application page.

universal_documents: KU Leuven standard admission application for an eligible programme
Institute of Philosophy application file: CV, motivation letter and the Institute of Philosophy academic reading and writing assignment
For the waiver request: an email to the Education and Students Office with the admission offer attached as a PDF, stating full name, student number, nationality and programme of admission

two_recommendation_letters.note: No recommendation letters are required for the Bachelor of Philosophy admission file at the Institute of Philosophy or for this waiver request, based on the official admission requirements and waiver pages. Letters of recommendation are requested for other KU Leuven awards such as Science@Leuven and ICP Connect, which are master's-level.

secondary_school_documents: High school diploma giving access to university-level education in the applicant's home country
Transcripts and full diploma documentation as part of the complete application file, per KU Leuven's requested-documents list for bachelor applicants
official_application_documents.document_language: Not specified on the award page. KU Leuven publishes a requested-documents page for degree applications; applicants should check the current language and translation requirements there.
official_application_documents.document_format: Admission documents are uploaded through the KU Leuven application tool. The waiver request is submitted by email with the admission offer attached as a PDF.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Part of the complete application file used for the admission decision; no separate transcript is published as a waiver-specific requirement.
official_application_documents.certified_translation_requirement: Not published on the award page. KU Leuven's requested-documents instructions for degree applications specify document language and translation requirements; these must be checked there.

selection_process.decision_maker: Education and Students Office of the KU Leuven Institute of Philosophy
selection_process.selection_type: Administrative first-come, first-served award; no competitive ranking
possible_stages: Admission decision by the Board of Admissions of the Institute of Philosophy (programme admission)
Check that the applicant holds an admission letter for an eligible programme
Check that the applicant's nationality is on the eligible list
Check that the waiver request is complete
Award of one of the three waivers to one of the first three eligible complete requests
selection_process.weighting_note: No weighting scheme is published. The waiver is not competitively weighted: the first three eligible applicants who submit a complete request by email are automatically awarded it. Academic assessment governs admission only, and the selection criteria of the waiver are stated to be the same as those of the corresponding programme.
selection_process.results_timing: No separate results publication date is published. The Institute states that the selection timing is linked to the admission process of the eligible programmes, and the 2026-2027 page noted that confirmed waivers are applied to the tuition invoice. Applicants should not expect a separate shortlisting round.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: No ranking, waiting list or reserve list is published for this waiver.

selection_criteria.additional_factors: Timeliness of the request: the first three eligible applicants who submit a complete request by email are awarded the waiver. The Institute states the waiver is intended for students from non-EEA countries in need of financial support, but the operative eligibility test is nationality against the DAC list; no income documentation is required.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor of Philosophy (Bachelor of Arts), 180 ECTS, Institute of Philosophy, KU Leuven
possible_awards: Bachelor of Philosophy (Abridged Programme of 102 ECTS) (Leuven)
Bachelor of Philosophy (Abridged Programme of 63 ECTS) (Leuven)
Master of Philosophy (Leuven) and Research Master of Philosophy (Leuven), also covered by this waiver but out of bachelor's scope
degree_outcome.degree_note: The waiver is attached to enrolment at the Institute of Philosophy. An academic bachelor's degree from this programme gives access to the Master of Philosophy and other master's programmes; KU Leuven notes that graduates are not yet ready for the labour market with the academic bachelor's alone.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: The Institute of Philosophy admission requirements do not publish a credit-transfer or recognition rule for this waiver. Applicants with prior credits should raise recognition with the Education and Students Office before requesting the waiver.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Reduced tuition fee of EUR 3,252.72 for a full-time 60-ECTS programme in academic year 2026-2027 (2027-2028 amount to be communicated). The standard non-EEA fee was EUR 9,493.90 and the EEA fee EUR 1,181.40 for the same 60 credits.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No application fee waiver for this award is published. The fee is charged for the admission application and is separate from the waiver.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: KU Leuven charges a fixed fee plus a variable fee per credit and recalculates the fee after the Individual Study Programme of the second semester is approved. The increased tuition fees remain applicable for the entire duration of the programme unless a partial waiver has been granted.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: KU Leuven tuition fees include affiliation with the collective accident insurance and civil liability insurance for study-related activities. Affiliation with the 'private life civil liability' insurance is an additional obligation for non-EEA students temporarily residing in Belgium.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: None published. The award carries no service bond or return-to-home-country obligation.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm that your nationality appears on the Institute of Philosophy eligible-nationality list (DAC least developed or other low income countries)
Secure and submit an admission application to the Bachelor of Philosophy through the KU Leuven application tool before the non-EEA admission deadline
Prepare the CV, motivation letter and the Institute of Philosophy academic reading and writing assignment
Take or arrange an English test (TOEFL 90 / IELTS 6.5 / Cambridge C1 176) unless you qualify for a test exemption
After the admission letter arrives, immediately email the Education and Students Office with the admission offer (PDF), full name, student number, nationality and programme
Re-check the current cycle's fee amount, because the reduced fee is republished every academic year
programme_comparison_fields: Award type: partial tuition fee waiver, not a living-allowance scholarship
Waiver value against the standard non-EEA fee: 3,252.72 vs 9,493.90 EUR per 60 ECTS (2026-2027)
Number of awards: three per academic year, first-come first-served
Restriction: non-EEA nationality on a DAC-derived country list
Requires prior admission, so the admission deadline is the effective gate
Duration: entire length of the programme for eligible DAC nationalities
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The motivation letter is an admission document, not a waiver document: it is assessed as part of the application file by the Board of Admissions alongside the academic reading and writing assignment. Write it as an academic fit statement for philosophy, since decisions on admission are based on the candidate's academic potential as demonstrated by the complete application file. There is no separate financial-need statement or 500-word financial motivation letter for this waiver, unlike the KU Leuven Faculty of Social Sciences waiver.
profile_fit_labels: Non-EEA student from a DAC least developed or other low income country
Wants an English-taught bachelor's degree in philosophy
Needs a tuition fee reduction rather than a living stipend
Can obtain an admission letter quickly and act immediately after it arrives
Self-funding or externally funded for living costs
common_mistakes: Assuming the award is a full scholarship with a living allowance - it is a tuition fee reduction only
Expecting a competitive academic ranking - the waiver is first-come first-served among three places
Applying for the waiver before receiving the admission letter, which invalidates the request
Assuming all non-EEA countries are eligible - lower-middle-income countries are excluded
Missing that the admission deadline (1 March for non-EEA applicants in the 2026-2027 cycle) is the real gate
Treating the published EUR 3,252.72 as a permanent figure - it is republished per academic year and was not yet published for 2027-2028

risk_flags.risk: First-come, first-served allocation of only three waivers
risk_flags.impact: An eligible applicant who submits later than the first three eligible requests receives nothing, regardless of academic strength
risk_flags.mitigation: Request the waiver by email immediately after the admission letter arrives, and confirm with the Education and Students Office whether any waiver remains

risk_flags.risk: Waiver requires a prior admission letter
risk_flags.impact: The effective deadline is the programme admission deadline, not the 20 September waiver deadline
risk_flags.mitigation: Submit the admission application as early as possible in the application window and treat the admission deadline as the binding date

risk_flags.risk: Nationality list is derived from the DAC list and can change
risk_flags.impact: A country can move between DAC income categories and lose or gain eligibility between cycles
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-read the eligible-nationality list on the current cycle page before applying; do not rely on a previous cycle's list

risk_flags.risk: Reduced fee amount is republished annually and the 2027-2028 figure is unpublished
risk_flags.impact: The financial benefit cannot be quantified for the 2027-2028 cycle until KU Leuven publishes the fee
risk_flags.mitigation: Check the Institute of Philosophy tuition fees page and the current cycle award page each academic year; treat EUR 3,252.72 as the 2026-2027 rate only

risk_flags.risk: Inconsistent official statements on waiver duration
risk_flags.impact: The catalogue page says one academic year while the Institute page says the entire duration of studies, so renewal is uncertain
risk_flags.mitigation: Ask the Education and Students Office to confirm the renewal rule in writing before enrolling

risk_flags.impact: A tuition-only award does not cover the roughly EUR 1,000+ per month of living costs in Belgium
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget separately for living costs; consider the Institute of Philosophy Study Support Allowance (tuition plus EUR 1,500) or external funding, noting that the Study Support Allowance is a separate award with its own closed application window

risk_flags.impact: The waiver cannot be transferred to another KU Leuven programme or faculty
risk_flags.mitigation: Only consider this award if the Bachelor of Philosophy (or its abridged variants) is the intended programme

risk_flags.impact: Links such as /scholarships/year/2027-2028/... will change every year and may break
risk_flags.mitigation: Use the stable catalogue page https://www.kuleuven.be/scholarships/year to locate the current cycle award page

Applicants who need a scholarship that can be applied for before admission is decided

image.logo_verification_method: The logo asset was fetched directly from KU Leuven's own corporate-style domain, stijl.kuleuven.be, which serves the logo file used in the header and print footer of every official kuleuven.be page, including this award page. The awarding body for this award is the KU Leuven Institute of Philosophy within KU Leuven, so the KU Leuven logo is the correct provider mark and is not a third-party or misattributed logo.

unverified_or_removed_claims: No award officially named 'KU Leuven International Scholarship' exists on kuleuven.be; the target name used in the assignment does not correspond to an official award title and was not recorded as such.

Ghent University publishes no bachelor's-level international scholarship: its funding overview for prospective students lists only Master Mind master's scholarships, VLIR-UOS ICP development-cooperation scholarships and Erasmus Mundus joint masters, and its reduced-tuition-fee route requires either Belgian nationality, EEA nationality or a non-EEA nationality condition met through at least 12 months of lawful residence in Belgium (a study or work residence permit does not count), which a newly arriving non-EEA student cannot satisfy.
The 2027-2028 reduced fee amount is not published by KU Leuven.

database_notes: Scheme chosen and why: the assignment target named a 'KU Leuven International Scholarship' and Ghent University undergraduate scholarship / tuition-waiver schemes. No award named 'KU Leuven International Scholarship' exists on kuleuven.be, and Ghent University publishes no bachelor's-level international scholarship, so the best-documented bachelor's-level non-EEA award in the KU Leuven catalogue was recorded instead.

Why this award over the alternatives: it is the only KU Leuven award in the official scholarship catalogue that (a) explicitly lists Bachelor's programmes under 'Degree type', (b) names a specific bachelor's programme (Bachelor of Philosophy, Leuven), (c) publishes an exact amount (EUR 3,252.72 for 2026-2027), (d) publishes an exact calendar deadline with a timezone, (e) publishes the number of awards (three), and (f) publishes a renewal rule tied to the DAC nationality list. All six items are confirmed on official KU Leuven domains.

Other KU Leuven awards were checked and excluded at bachelor's level: Science@Leuven Scholarship (Master's only), Faculty of Science Fee Waiver (Master's only), Anne Hart Scholarship (Master's only, Faculty of Arts), Faculty of Social Sciences Partial Tuition Fee Waiver (Master's only), ICP Connect Scholarship (Master's only, 50 awards), Bolashak International Scholarship (Master's and PhD only).

Ghent University was evaluated and excluded: its 'Funding your studies' page for prospective students lists only master's-level schemes (Master Mind, VLIR-UOS ICP development cooperation, Erasmus Mundus joint masters). Ghent's reduced tuition fee route is the Flemish study-grant or near-study-grant rate, which requires Belgian nationality, EEA nationality, or a non-EEA applicant who satisfies the Department of Study grants nationality conditions - and per Flanders.be a non-EEA national must have been lawfully resident in Belgium for at least 12 months, with residence permits granted to study or work not counting. Ghent's mandatory reduced contribution and 100% higher-tuition waivers for OESO/DAC developing countries apply to its Master programmes and English preparatory programmes, not to bachelor programmes.

bachelor_requirement is set to false because this award funds a bachelor's programme and the qualifying prior qualification is a secondary-school diploma rather than a completed bachelor's degree; the secondary/high-school conditions are expressed in final_year_bachelor_allowed, final_year_condition and equivalent_degree_note, as the contract directs for bachelor's awards.

Amount provenance: the reduced fee of EUR 3,252.72 and the standard fees of EUR 9,493.90 (non-EEA) and EUR 1,181.40 (EEA) for 60 credits in 2026-2027 are taken from the Institute of Philosophy tuition fees page and corroborated by the 2026-2027 award page. The EUR 6,241.18 difference is a derived comparison and is explicitly not presented as an official award value.
No 'total value' of the award is computed: the waiver is a per-academic-year conditional tuition reduction, not a lump-sum grant, and the official sources publish no total.

Status: the 2026-2027 cycle closed on 20 September 2026, so an application for that intake is no longer possible; the 2027-2028 cycle window opened on 1 October 2026 and closes on 20 September 2027 at 01:00 (GMT+1), which is why the record is marked OPEN with that date.

Two official KU Leuven pages state the duration differently. The scholarship catalogue page says 'One academic year'; the Institute of Philosophy tuition fees page says award holders from low-income countries keep the waiver 'for the entire duration of their studies at the Institute of Philosophy'. Because every nationality on the eligible list is a DAC least developed or other low income country, the practical reading is renewal for the full programme, but the discrepancy is flagged rather than resolved.

The 'three available scholarships' figure is the published number, but the 2026-2027 award page notes that, thanks to donations, partial tuition fee waivers were granted to all eligible students for academic year 2026-2027, so the effective number of awards can exceed three.

The study-support allowance described on the Institute of Philosophy site (full tuition fee reimbursement plus a EUR 1,500 lump sum, applications for 2026-2027 closed) is a separate award from the partial tuition fee waiver recorded here and is not included in the funding fields of this record.

The waiver's eligibility depends on admission, so the operative application gate is the programme admission deadline rather than the waiver deadline. The non-EEA admission deadline for the Institute of Philosophy programmes was 1 March in the 2026-2027 cycle; the 2027-2028 admission windows had not been published for all programmes at the time of verification and are listed as items requiring a programme check.

KU Leuven charges a processing fee for admission applications. The fee is not published on the award page and is not stated as a figure here; recognised refugees in Belgium are among the exempt categories published by KU Leuven.
No photo is recorded for this award. The award page carries an image on the KU Leuven domain, but its subject and licence could not be confirmed from the official source, so image_url is null.

Cycle-specific award URLs contain the academic year in the path and change annually; https://www.kuleuven.be/scholarships/year is the stable catalogue entry point and is recorded as the official_updates_url.
